paper_title: Aerobic Oxidation of Propargyl Alcohol: A Convenient Method for the Synthesis of Propiolaldehyde

questions.question: In this paper, what does the abbreviation 'DCE' refer to?
What is the chemical structure of compound 1 (propiolaldehyde) as shown in the paper?
What solvent, catalysts (including mol%), oxygen pressure, and temperature were used for the aerobic oxidation of propargyl alcohol to propiolaldehyde in the reported procedure?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Solvent: p-xylene; catalysts/additives: Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (5 mol%), TEMPO (3 mol%), NaCl (5 mol%); oxidant: O2 at atmospheric pressure (1 atm); temperature: room temperature.

questions.question: Which gave the higher yield for preparation of propiolaldehyde, the aerobic Fe(NO3)3/TEMPO method reported here or Sauer's CrO3 oxidation, and what yields are reported for each?
questions.ground_truth_answer: The aerobic Fe(NO3)3/TEMPO method in this paper gave the higher yield: 54% (30.06 g, purified). Sauer's reported CrO3 oxidation gave 35–41% yield.
